all_quotes.quote: Using the the CO ($J$=3–2) data from the exoALMA Large Program encompassing 15 disks, we constructed two-dimensional (2D) maps of centroid velocity, line width, and peak intensity
We provide an overview of how the observed velocity and intensity distributions deviate from those expected for a Keplerian rotating disk
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.
the data from $^{12}$CO ($J$=3–2), which have high S/N, are mainly used
The images in $^{13}$CO ($J$=3–2) and CS ($J$=7–6) are included in the Appendix

images with beam sizes of $0.15\ensuremath{''}$ or $0.30\ensuremath{''}$ and velocity resolutions of 28 m s$^{-1}$, 100 m s$^{-1}$, or 200 m s$^{-1}$ are utilized
obtaining $\langle$$z/r$$\rangle$=0.28 and 0.16 for $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO, respectively

While a synthesized beam size of $0.15\ensuremath{''}$ and a velocity resolution of 100 m s$^{-1}$ are used as the baseline

following the analysis method presented in (cite: exoALMA_discminer)
single-component (Gaussian, bell) and double-component (double-bell, double-Gaussian) fitting kernels were all tested and the one that best reproduced the observed spectral profiles was selected
Residual maps were created by subtracting the model disk obtained from spectral fitting using DISCMINER
we roughly classify the sources into three categories according to the spatial distribution of the residuals: (1) spiral, (2) arc- or ring-like, and (3) other types

We find that all targets exhibit large-scale deviations from smooth Keplerian disks
Non-axisymmetric spiral-arm features are detected or suggested in five disks (CQ Tau, MWC 758, HD 135344B, HD 34282, and SY Cha)
This 2D atlas suggests that kinematic substructures are ubiquitous in large ($\gtrsim 100$ au) protoplanetary disks
and are preferentially found in Herbig Ae/Fe systems
